topSignals.title: JPMorgan resets Bloom Energy PT from $346 to $314, keeps Overweight — BE slides 1.65% while market gains
topSignals.text: — JPMorgan analyst Mark Strouse trimmed his Bloom Energy price target post-Q2 earnings to $314 (from the $346 set at the July 22 upgrade), maintaining Overweight. The cut reflects revised delivery-timing assumptions on Oracle Project Jupiter and the AEP Wyoming developer loss flagged by TD Cowen. Despite the PT reduction, Strouse keeps the bullish rating — implying a ~31% upside from today's close of $239.38. That close represents a -1.65% session on a day when broader markets gained ground, suggesting ongoing project-execution anxiety rather than fundamental deterioration. Zacks independently rates BE as #1 (Strong Buy) with a 3.9% consensus EPS revision upward over the last 30 days. JPMorgan PT reset — Yahoo Finance / TheStreet | Zacks Bloom Energy drops despite market | StockAnalysis.com

topSignals.title: Oracle Project Jupiter: dismiss-motion response due August 11 — permit fate decided within 24 hours
topSignals.text: — The New Mexico Environment Department hearing officer Max Shepherd has ordered project developer Yucca Growth Infrastructure to submit its response to New Energy Economy's motion to dismiss the air quality permit application by tomorrow, August 11. If the hearing officer grants the dismiss motion, Oracle cannot simply refile — it would need an entirely new fuel supply solution (the twice-denied Energy Transfer pipeline route is closed) before refiling. Developer attorneys cited $325M/month carrying costs as justification for expedited handling; a dismissal freezes proceedings entirely. The September 14 public hearing remains scheduled but depends on the dismiss ruling. This is the single highest-risk near-term event for the global announced SOFC AI datacenter pipeline (Oracle/Project Jupiter = 2.45 GW, ~16% of total announced capacity). KANW / Source NM rescheduling context | Santa Fe New Mexican — dismiss motion filing | ABQ Journal

topSignals.title: Two new system-level SOFC papers identified: SO-FREE CHP achieves 60–77% electrical efficiency at >90% utilization factor; SOFC vs H2-ICE institutional TEA sets SOFC LCOE at $33.5¢/kWh
topSignals.text: — (a) The EU Horizon 2020 SO-FREE project, published in Energies (April 2025, DOI: 10.3390/en18092273), demonstrates a low-emission, fuel-flexible, modular SOFC-CHP system achieving a system utilization factor >90%, electrical efficiency 60–77%, and heat recovery >60% — all in an architecture explicitly designed to minimize component count and reduce plant cost. Interchangeable stack types tested; Aspen Plus simulation verified. LCOE flag: the 60–77% electrical range with >60% heat recovery is the widest validated efficiency band for a modular SOFC-CHP system published to date and directly supports the CHP heat-monetization credit in LCOE modeling. (b) A ScienceDirect comparative TEA (Fuel journal, pii S0016236125024056, Sept 2025) benchmarks SOFC-CHP vs. hydrogen-fueled ICE-CHP at the University of Alberta: SOFC LCOE = $33.5¢/kWh, HICE LCOE = $20.1¢/kWh — SOFC carries a 67% cost premium but delivers essentially zero NOx (vs. >4 tonnes NOx/yr for H2-ICE), confirming regulatory compliance value. LCOE flag. Energies SO-FREE | ScienceDirect SOFC vs H2-ICE

Deep Atomic MK60 SMR: DOE nuclear-AI data center proposal at Idaho National Laboratory — Deep Atomic submitted a proposal to DOE's Office of Nuclear Energy for what it calls the "nation's first" fully integrated nuclear-powered AI data center campus at INL, using its MK60 light water SMR (60 MWe / 200 MWth). Consortium includes Clayco, Gleeds, Paragon Energy Solutions, and others. The phased approach uses grid, geothermal, and solar power in the first 24–36 months while the MK60 completes design certification, fabrication, and commissioning — meaning no nuclear power on-site before ~2029 at the earliest. This is not new news (proposal submitted late 2025/early 2026) but surfaced prominently in today's coverage. Competitive implication: adds yet another modular nuclear concept targeting AI data centers, but with the same 2029+ delivery horizon that leaves SOFC unchallenged through the current AI buildout. items.text: SO-FREE Project: Low-Emission, Fuel-Flexible, Modular SOFC-CHP System Architecture (Energies, MDPI, April 2025, DOI: 10.3390/en18092273) — EU Horizon 2020 project delivering a reference SOFC-CHP architecture with interchangeable stack types, validated via Aspen Plus simulation. Key system-level figures: utilization factor >90%, electrical efficiency 60–77%, effective heat recovery >60%. Minimized-component design explicitly targets cost reduction. LCOE-relevant: the 60–77% electrical efficiency range, combined with >60% heat recovery, is the broadest validated system-level efficiency band for a modular SOFC-CHP; supports the CHP heat-monetization credit across the full efficiency uncertainty range in LCOE sensitivity analysis. Energies — SO-FREE

Comparative TEA: SOFC-CHP vs. H2-ICE-CHP for Institutional Energy Management (Fuel / ScienceDirect, Sept 2025, pii S0016236125024056) — Real-data comparison at the University of Alberta. SOFC: capex $280M, opex $66.3M/yr, LCOE $33.5¢/kWh, near-zero NOx. H2-ICE: capex $140M, opex $24.25M/yr, LCOE $20.1¢/kWh, but >4 tonnes NOx/yr. Conclusion: HICE is currently more economical; SOFC preferred for institutions with hard decarbonization mandates. LCOE-relevant: SOFC institutional LCOE benchmark at $33.5¢/kWh (hydrogen feed). In natural gas mode and with CHP heat credit, commercial-scale SOFC LCOE is materially lower. Confirms NOx avoidance (regulatory compliance value) as a secondary SOFC advantage where local air quality standards apply. ScienceDirect SOFC vs H2-ICE

Improving Low-Load Efficiency of Marine SOFC Powertrains via Hot Standby Operation (IOP Journal of the Electrochemical Society, 2026, DOI: 10.1149/1945-7111/ae7479) — Marine context, but system-level engineering insight: efficient hot standby operation during low-load periods recovers efficiency losses from partial-load operation in SOFC module arrays. For data center applications requiring SOFC load-following (variable AI workloads), the hot standby architecture is directly transferable — relevant to multi-module SOFC systems designed for dynamic AI inference load profiles. Not TEA/LCOE, but relevant for system design and degradation modeling under non-steady-state operation. IOPscience

lcoe.text: SO-FREE electrical efficiency range 60–77% with >60% heat recovery (new): Broadens the efficiency uncertainty band in the LCOE sensitivity model. Base case (60% electrical, 24% heat capture) remains intact; add upper-bound scenario at 77% electrical with 60% heat recovery — this represents best-in-class modular system performance and yields the most favorable SOFC LCOE. System utilization factor >90% also reduces capacity factor uncertainty in the model. Energies SO-FREE

SOFC institutional CHP LCOE benchmark: $33.5¢/kWh on hydrogen (new): At hydrogen feed prices, SOFC LCOE is 67% higher than H2-ICE ($20.1¢/kWh). On natural gas, SOFC LCOE is materially lower (carry-forward ScienceDirect data-center LCOE study: $130–225/MWh = $13–22.5¢/kWh). The delta quantifies the hydrogen-vs-NG fuel premium: switching from NG to H2 roughly doubles SOFC LCOE under current H2 economics. Maintains NG as the defensible fuel assumption through at least 2029. ScienceDirect SOFC vs H2-ICE

JPMorgan PT cut to $314 — implied BE capex trajectory note: JPMorgan's PT reduction from $346 to $314 post-Q2 reflects delayed Project Jupiter and AEP delivery, not a change in long-run manufacturing cost outlook. However, if large orders slip 1–2 years, Bloom's 2 GW/yr Fremont run rate may not be sustained at high utilization, slowing the manufacturing cost learning curve. Hold current base-case capex at $5,500–6,000/kW (pre-ITC) for 2026–2028 modeling; update on Q3 earnings (October). Yahoo Finance JPMorgan
